as_written_in_papers.quote: Results revealed that the patient had a heterozygous c.1535A > T mutation on exon 4 in the nucleotide-binding domain of NOD2, while her parents did not.
Analysis of the protein variant revealed that the mutation was D512V (p.Asp512Val) (Fig. 6).

cases.statement: One person: a Japanese girl (identity BLAU-ID0138), heterozygous, with infantile papules, granulomatous dermatitis on biopsy and refractory bilateral granulomatous panuveitis with multifocal choroiditis; no arthritis.

people.label: patient
people.other_allele: not applicable (autosomal dominant); no second NOD2 variant reported
people.key_phenotypes: papules on legs and hands from early infancy; anterior uveitis at 5 years progressing to bilateral granulomatous panuveitis with posterior synechiae; bilateral multifocal choroiditis with macular scar; noncaseating epithelioid cell granulomas on skin biopsy; no arthritis (normal MRI of extremities)

quotes.quote: During early infancy, a Japanese girl developed papules on her legs and the dorsum of her hands.
At age 5, she developed both conjunctival hyperemia and photophobia in her left eye; she was diagnosed with anterior uveitis, which was effectively treated using localized therapy.
The fundus was characterized by bilateral multifocal choroiditis presenting as creamy yellow lesions, and a scar was seen in the macular region of her left eye (Fig. 2).
A skin biopsy from papules on her leg indicated granulomatous dermatitis (Figs. 1b and c and 3).
Magnetic resonance imaging of the extremities was carried out to evaluate the presence of arthritis; no abnormalities were detected.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Skin granulomas and granulomatous panuveitis fit the disease as the authors describe it, but arthritis, the commonest manifestation, was absent. ANA and RF were negative and immunological tests normal; a mycobacterial stain of the granulomas was negative. Chronic granulomatous disease was not formally excluded (no respiratory burst assay). Only NOD2 was sequenced (all 12 exons); no other genes were tested.

quotes.quote: Our patient did not show any symptoms of arthritis.
However, the most common manifestation of EOS/BS is symmetric and usually painless polyarthritis [19].
Her immunological tests were normal, and there were no episodes of recurrent or severe bacterial or fungal infection.
Therefore, no additional tests, such as a flow cytometric dihydrorhodamine neutrophil respiratory burst assay, were performed to rule out chronic granulomatous disease.

The PAB antibody detected several signals of round bodies within the sarcoid granulomas and in lesions infiltrated by inflammatory cells, while no positive signal was observed using the LAM antibody as control (Fig. 4).

segregation.statement: No affected relatives are described. Both parents were tested and do not carry the variant; their clinical status is not stated.

quotes.quote: Genetic analyses were performed of both the patient’s and her parents’ NOD2 genes.
No such mutation was found in her parents (black arrows).

de_novo.statement: Both parents were Sanger-sequenced (all 12 NOD2 exons) and lacked the variant. Parentage confirmation is not reported.

quotes.quote: Genomic DNA was extracted from the peripheral blood of the patient and her parents, and all 12 exons of the NOD2 gene, including exon-intron boundaries, were amplified by polymerase chain reaction and sequenced by Sanger method.
Results revealed that the patient had a heterozygous c.1535A > T mutation on exon 4 in the nucleotide-binding domain of NOD2, while her parents did not.
Genetic analyses revealed that the patient had a NOD2 heterozygous D512V mutation that was novel and not present in either of her parents.

functional.statement: Construct assay: NF-kB luciferase reporter in HEK293T cells transfected with the NOD2 D512V expression construct, with and without MDP. Controls: mock vector and wild-type NOD2; R334W and H496L as positive controls. Result as stated: increased basal NF-kB activity, further increased after MDP stimulation. The result sentence cites reference [18] (Matsuda et al. 2020) and no data figure for the assay appears in this paper.

quotes.quote: HEK293T cells (1 × 10^5) were cotransfected with 30 ng of the expression construct of the NOD2 variant together with an NF-κB reporter plasmid.
NF-κB activity was measured after 12 h of incubation either with or without 5 µg/mL MDP.
A mock vector and the wild-type NOD2 were used as controls [1]; R334W and H496L were used as positive controls [1].
An in vitro assessment of the mutation indicated an increased basal NF-κB activity that increased further after MDP stimulation [18], demonstrating a strong association with EOS/BS.
Functional analysis showed elevated background activity and augmented activity after ligand stimulation, demonstrating a strong association with EOS/BS.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense (predicted p.Asp485Val on NP_001357395.1), in the nucleotide-binding domain per the authors. The authors describe EOS/BS NOD2 mutations as gain-of-function (gene-level statement), consistent with dominant inheritance.

quotes.quote: A gain-of-function mutation in the nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-containing protein 2 (NOD2) gene has been demonstrated in this disease; however, little is known about the relationship between the activation of NOD2 and the pathophysiology of EOS/BS.

NOD2 mutations in patients with EOS/BS enhance the self-oligomerization of NOD2, leading to augmented NOD2 activity even in the absence of the ligand MDP; further increases in activity by the addition of ligands represent gain-of-function mutations, consistent with the dominant mode of inheritance of the granulomatous disease [10, 11].

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it a novel D512V mutation and, from the functional result, a strong association with EOS/BS that confirmed the diagnosis; no ACMG criteria are given.

quotes.quote: The mutant NOD2 showed a similar activation pattern to EOS/BS, thus confirming her diagnosis.
In summary, we presented a case of EOS/BS with a novel D512V mutation in the NOD2 gene.

concerns: Legacy numbering: the paper writes c.1535A>T / D512V (p.Asp512Val) with no transcript; the batch places it as NM_001370466.1:c.1454A>T, predicted p.(Asp485Val). The 81-nt and 27-residue offsets match the older NM_022162 numbering (protein_check: differs, stated D512V, predicted D485V). The panel should confirm the placement.

Same person reported elsewhere: the paper states 'This patient is the same as the D512V case reported in reference number 18' (Matsuda et al. 2020, Ann Rheum Dis, PMID 32647028). If that paper is in the corpus, its D512V case must be merged with BLAU-ID0138, not counted as a second case.

The paper contradicts the earlier report: it says reference 18 wrongly listed polyarthritis and renal calcification for this patient ('In fact, the statement that polyarthritis and renal calcification were present is an error made by the authors of reference number 18'). Phenotypes taken from PMID 32647028 for this person should not be used.
The functional result is cited to reference [18] and no assay data are shown in this paper; the panel may want to see the data in the cited source.
De novo: both parents tested negative, but parentage confirmation is not reported.
Atypical presentation without arthritis; chronic granulomatous disease was not formally excluded by a respiratory burst assay.
notes_for_panel: Strongest of these four candidates on paper: de novo by Sanger testing of both parents (parentage not confirmed) and an NF-kB reporter assay in HEK293T showing raised basal and MDP-stimulated activity with stated controls. Check first that this patient is not double-counted with the D512V case in Matsuda 2020 (PMID 32647028), which this paper says is the same person with erroneous phenotypes. Legacy numbering c.1535A>T / D512V = MANE c.1454A>T / D485V per the batch.
